note: storms: HURDAT2 (NOAA/NHC, public domain), hurricanes only. eruptions/quakes/weather: authored from general knowledge — VERIFY dates, magnitudes, tolls against Smithsonian GVP, USGS/ISC, and period press before v0.1.

eruptions.name: Sakurajima
eruptions.line: Sakurajima in eruption; lava reaches the sea at Kurokami. Kagoshima sweeps ash.

eruptions.name: Hekla
eruptions.line: Hekla erupts after a century's silence. Ash to thirty kilometres; the column is seen from Scotland.

eruptions.name: Cumbre Vieja
eruptions.line: The San Juan eruption opens on La Palma's Cumbre Vieja on the saint's day. Thirty-seven days; lava to the western coast.

eruptions.name: Mauna Loa
eruptions.line: Mauna Loa's largest eruption in a lifetime. Lava crosses the coast road in three hours.

eruptions.name: Etna
eruptions.line: Etna's longest flank eruption in living memory begins. Milo threatened.

eruptions.name: Lamington
eruptions.line: Mount Lamington explodes without warning. The Higaturu district is gone; 2,942 dead.

eruptions.name: Kelud
eruptions.line: Kelud erupts in East Java, VEI 4. Ash on the rice terraces from Kediri to Malang.

eruptions.name: Myōjin-shō
eruptions.line: A submarine volcano surfaces south of Tokyo and destroys the survey ship sent to study it. No survivors.

eruptions.name: Mount Spurr
eruptions.line: Spurr erupts; a quarter-inch of ash on Anchorage by afternoon.

eruptions.name: Ruapehu
eruptions.line: Ruapehu's crater lake bursts. The lahar takes the Tangiwai rail bridge with the Wellington express on it.

eruptions.name: Kīlauea
eruptions.line: Kīlauea's east rift opens through the cane fields of lower Puna — twenty-four vents in eighty-eight days. The coast from Kalapana to Kapoho evacuated.

eruptions.name: Bezymianny
eruptions.line: Bezymianny, the Kamchatka volcano the maps called extinct, blows out its south-east flank. Ash column to thirty-five kilometres; the Soviets report it as a scientific matter.

eruptions.name: Agung
eruptions.line: Agung erupts on Bali after a century's rest. Pyroclastic flows through the villages of the east; a second eruption on 16 May. 1,584 dead. The sulphur is in the stratosphere by summer.

eruptions.name: Taal
eruptions.line: Taal erupts through the lake on the south-west of Volcano Island. Base surges cross the water into the lakeshore villages; about 190 dead.

eruptions.name: Kelud
eruptions.line: Kelud erupts in East Java. The crater lake goes down the valleys as lahar; more than 200 dead. Tunnels to drain the lake are ordered.

eruptions.name: Fernandina
eruptions.line: Fernandina, in the Galápagos, explodes and its caldera floor drops three hundred metres. The blast is recorded on infrasound across the hemisphere; ash to 350 kilometres. Nobody lives there.

eruptions.name: Arenal
eruptions.line: Arenal, thought dormant, erupts in Costa Rica at half past seven in the morning. Tabacón, Pueblo Nuevo and San Luis buried; 87 dead.

eruptions.name: Nyiragongo
eruptions.line: Nyiragongo's lava lake drains in under an hour through fissures in the crater wall. Lava at sixty kilometres an hour through Kibati and Moniki; at least 50 dead.

eruptions.name: Mount St. Helens
eruptions.line: Mount St. Helens' north flank gives way at 8:32 in the morning. Ash to 24 kilometres; four inches on Yakima by noon, dark in Spokane. 57 dead; four billion board feet of timber; wheat and orchards under ash across the interior. $1.1 billion.

eruptions.name: El Chichón
eruptions.line: El Chichón, in Chiapas, erupts three times in a week. Nine villages gone; about 1,900 dead. Seven million tonnes of sulphur dioxide into the stratosphere — the cloud circles the earth in three weeks.

eruptions.name: Galunggung
eruptions.line: Galunggung erupts in West Java and does not stop for months. On 24 June a British Airways 747 loses all four engines in the ash cloud and glides for sixteen minutes before they restart; Singapore Airlines loses three on 14 July. Tens of thousands evacuated; 18 dead.

eruptions.name: Nevado del Ruiz
eruptions.line: A small eruption of Nevado del Ruiz melts the summit ice. The lahar reaches Armero, forty-eight kilometres away, at half past eleven at night. Of 29,000 people, more than 20,000 do not survive it. The hazard map had been published in October.

eruptions.name: Lake Nyos
eruptions.line: Lake Nyos, in the Cameroon highlands, overturns in the night and releases its dissolved carbon dioxide. The gas moves down the valleys; 1,746 people and 3,500 head of cattle dead within twenty-five kilometres. No eruption in the ordinary sense.

eruptions.name: Redoubt
eruptions.line: Redoubt erupts across Cook Inlet from Anchorage. On the second day a new KLM 747 flies into the cloud and loses all four engines, recovering them 14,000 feet lower. Lahars twice reach the Drift River oil terminal. $160 million.

eruptions.name: Kelud
eruptions.line: Kelud again, VEI 4, after twenty-four years. Twenty to thirty centimetres of tephra on the villages; 500 homes and 50 schools down under the weight; 32 dead.

eruptions.name: Unzen
eruptions.line: Unzen's growing dome collapses at ten past four in the afternoon. The pyroclastic flow runs the Mizunashi valley to Kita-Kamikoba; 43 dead, among them the Kraffts and Harry Glicken, and the journalists who had followed them.

eruptions.name: Pinatubo
eruptions.line: Pinatubo's climactic eruption, VEI 6, the largest in living memory. Column to 35 kilometres; a typhoon arrives the same afternoon and the wet ash brings down roofs across Central Luzon. 847 dead; Clark Air Base abandoned; 800 square kilometres of rice under ash. The sulphur dioxide load in the stratosphere is the largest ever measured; the world cools half a degree the following year.

eruptions.name: Cerro Hudson
eruptions.line: Hudson erupts in Chilean Patagonia; Plinian from 12 August. Ash over 150,000 square kilometres of Chile and Argentina, to the Falklands and South Georgia. Half the sheep of Santa Cruz province lost to the ash and the winter.

eruptions.name: Mayon
eruptions.line: Mayon erupts without warning. Pyroclastic flows across the farmed slopes of the east side; 79 dead, most of them in the fields.

eruptions.name: Rabaul
eruptions.line: Tavurvur and Vulcan erupt together on opposite sides of Rabaul harbour. Thirty thousand people left in the night on the warning of the observatory; the airport gone and the town under ash. Five dead.

eruptions.name: Merapi
eruptions.line: Merapi's dome collapses at a quarter past ten. The nuée goes six kilometres down the Boyong into Turgo; 64 dead.

eruptions.name: Soufrière Hills
eruptions.line: Soufrière Hills, in eruption since July 1995, sends pyroclastic flows across the north-east of Montserrat; 19 dead. Plymouth, evacuated last year, will not be reoccupied; the airport is destroyed. Two-thirds of the island closed.

eruptions.name: Nyiragongo
eruptions.line: Nyiragongo opens a thirteen-kilometre fissure on its south flank and the lava runs into Goma. Thirteen per cent of the city under it, the airport runway cut, 120,000 without homes; about 245 dead.

eruptions.name: Reventador
eruptions.line: Reventador, on the Amazon slope, erupts after twenty-six years with no warning. Column to seventeen kilometres; Quito dark by afternoon and its airport closed ten days. Lahars break the trans-Ecuadorian pipeline.

eruptions.name: Manam
eruptions.line: Manam, off the Madang coast, in eruption from October. The island's 9,600 people taken to the mainland. The paroxysm of 27 January reaches 24 kilometres; the villages and gardens of the east side are gone. Five dead.

eruptions.name: Chaitén
eruptions.line: Chaitén erupts in southern Chile — rhyolite, the first in the historical record. Column to thirty kilometres, ash across Argentina; the town of 4,200 evacuated by sea, and in May the river takes half of it. One dead in the evacuation.

eruptions.name: Eyjafjallajökull
eruptions.line: Eyjafjallajökull erupts through its ice cap. Fine ash over the North Atlantic; twenty countries close their airspace from 15 to 20 April. Ten million passengers grounded — the greatest interruption of European aviation since 1945.

eruptions.name: Merapi
eruptions.line: Merapi erupts; the explosion of 5 November is the largest in a century. 350,000 evacuated; Yogyakarta airport closed; 386 dead, most of them under pyroclastic flows.

eruptions.name: Puyehue–Cordón Caulle
eruptions.line: Cordón Caulle erupts in the Chilean lakes. Bariloche under ash and without power; flights across the south of the continent stopped, and — a fortnight later — across Australia and New Zealand as the cloud goes round. 750,000 sheep on ashed pasture in Argentina.

eruptions.name: Nabro
eruptions.line: Nabro erupts in the Eritrean Afar, a volcano with no historical record. Ash to fourteen kilometres; the highest sulphur dioxide injection yet seen by satellite. Flights across the Red Sea and the Horn suspended; 7 dead, 12,000 displaced.

eruptions.name: Sinabung
eruptions.line: Sinabung's dome collapses in the morning. Pyroclastic flows reach Sukameriah, inside the exclusion zone, where people had gone back; 16 dead.

eruptions.name: Kelud
eruptions.line: Kelud erupts at ten to eleven at night, VEI 4. Ash on seven airports from Bandung to Surabaya; 76,000 evacuated; 12,000 buildings damaged; 3 dead.

eruptions.name: Ontake
eruptions.line: Ontake, a beginner's mountain a hundred kilometres from Nagoya, erupts steam and ash without seismic warning at 11:52 on a fine Saturday. 63 dead on the summit trails.

eruptions.name: Calbuco
eruptions.line: Calbuco erupts with little warning in the evening, then again after midnight. Column to fifteen kilometres; 5,000 evacuated; flights across Chile and Argentina cancelled. No deaths.

eruptions.name: Kīlauea
eruptions.line: Kīlauea's east rift opens through Leilani Estates and runs to the sea for three months. Kapoho and Vacationland gone under lava; Green Lake boiled away; the geothermal plant shut; 700 homes. $800 million.

eruptions.name: Fuego
eruptions.line: Fuego's pyroclastic flows come down on San Miguel Los Lotes and El Rodeo at midday. At least 190 dead, 256 unaccounted for; La Aurora airport closed under ash; 21,000 acres of farmland lost.

eruptions.name: Anak Krakatau
eruptions.line: Anak Krakatau's south-west flank slides into the Sunda Strait at 21:38 and the wave reaches the Banten and Lampung coasts with no warning. 426 dead, 14,000 injured; the volcano two-thirds gone.

eruptions.name: Whakaari
eruptions.line: Whakaari erupts at 14:11 with 47 people on the crater floor, most of them from a cruise ship. 22 dead; 25 burned.

eruptions.name: Taal
eruptions.line: Taal erupts, the first since 1977. Ash on Manila; NAIA closed, 516 flights; 70,000 in evacuation centres. Crops on 2,700 hectares and 6,000 fish cages in the lake lost. 39 dead, one of them to the eruption itself.

eruptions.name: La Soufrière
eruptions.line: La Soufrière erupts on St Vincent at 8:41 in the morning. 16,000 evacuated from the north of the island the day before; ash on Barbados by the 11th; most of the island's crops lost. No deaths.

eruptions.name: Nyiragongo
eruptions.line: Nyiragongo again, in the evening. Lava to the northern edge of Goma; 17 villages and 1,000 homes gone, the N2 road cut; 400,000 leave the city. 32 dead.

eruptions.name: Cumbre Vieja
eruptions.line: The Cumbre Vieja opens on La Palma for eighty-five days. A thousand hectares under lava, Todoque gone, 3,000 buildings, a third of the banana terraces of the west coast. 7,000 displaced, one dead. €843 million.

eruptions.name: Semeru
eruptions.line: Semeru's dome collapses after heavy rain at ten to three in the afternoon. Pyroclastic flows and lahars through the villages of Lumajang; 69 dead, 5,200 homes; 10,600 displaced.

eruptions.name: Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai
eruptions.line: Hunga Tonga erupts in the late afternoon and the plume goes to 58 kilometres, above the stratosphere. The pressure wave circles the earth; tsunami on Tongatapu, and in Peru. Tonga's cable cut. Seven dead. 146 million tonnes of water into the stratosphere — not sulphur.

quakes.name: Aleutian Islands
quakes.line: Aleutian earthquake, M8.6. The tsunami reaches Hilo five hours later, unannounced. 167 dead — most of them in Hawaii.

quakes.name: Samaná Bay
quakes.line: Earthquake M8.0 off the Samaná peninsula. The tsunami takes Matanzas; 1,800 dead.

quakes.name: Ancash
quakes.line: Ancash earthquake in the Peruvian Andes. Landslides bury the valleys; 1,400 dead.

quakes.name: Nankai
quakes.line: Nankai earthquake, M8.1. Tsunami along the Kii coast; 1,362 dead, 36,000 homes gone.

quakes.name: Fukui
quakes.line: Fukui earthquake, M6.8. The city, rebuilt after the war, is flattened again. 5,131 dead; 63,000 homes.

quakes.name: Ashgabat
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.3 under Ashkhabad. The Soviet press reports damage. The toll — 110,000 — will be a state secret for forty years.

quakes.name: Khait
quakes.line: Khait earthquake, M7.5, in the Tajik SSR. Landslides bury the valleys; 12,000 dead. Moscow says nothing.

quakes.name: Ambato
quakes.line: Ambato earthquake, M6.5. Mountain towns buried by landslides; 6,000 dead.

quakes.name: Assam–Tibet
quakes.line: Assam–Tibet earthquake, M8.6, among the largest ever recorded. Whole hillsides into the Brahmaputra; 1,530 dead. The river dams, then breaks.

quakes.name: Jucuapa
quakes.line: Jucuapa earthquake in El Salvador. The town levelled; 1,100 dead.

quakes.name: Tokachi
quakes.line: Tokachi earthquake, M8.1, off Hokkaido. The tsunami takes 2,400 homes along the coast.

quakes.name: Kern County
quakes.line: Kern County earthquake, M7.5 — the largest in the lower forty-eight in fifty years. Tehachapi in ruins; the Southern Pacific tunnels collapsed.

quakes.name: Kamchatka
quakes.line: Kamchatka earthquake, M9.0. Tsunami across the Pacific; Hilo flooded again. Severo-Kurilsk erased, 2,300 dead — Moscow does not report it.

quakes.name: Yenice–Gönen
quakes.line: Yenice–Gönen earthquake, M7.3, south of the Marmara. 1,070 dead.

quakes.name: Orléansville
quakes.line: Orléansville earthquake, M6.7. 1,243 dead in the Chélif valley.

quakes.name: Agadir
quakes.line: Earthquake under Agadir, shallow, a little before midnight. The kasbah and the new town both down; 12,000 dead in a city of 40,000.

quakes.name: Valdivia
quakes.line: Earthquake M9.5 off southern Chile — the largest ever instrumentally recorded. Waves of 25 metres on the coast; Hilo flooded fifteen hours later, 61 dead there; 142 dead in Japan the next day. Valdivia four-tenths gone.

quakes.name: Buin Zahra
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.1 in the Qazvin plain west of Tehran. 21,000 mud-brick houses down in 31 villages; 12,225 dead.

quakes.name: Skopje
quakes.line: Earthquake under Skopje at 5:17 in the morning. Twenty seconds; four-fifths of the city gone, 1,070 dead, 200,000 without shelter.

quakes.name: Alaska
quakes.line: Earthquake M9.2 in Prince William Sound, Good Friday evening. Valdez and Seward take the wave; the Turnagain bluffs slide into the inlet; 139 dead from Kodiak to Crescent City.

quakes.name: Tashkent
quakes.line: Earthquake under central Tashkent, shallow, before dawn. Some 80,000 adobe homes gone and 300,000 without housing; Moscow reports 15 dead.

quakes.name: Dasht-e Bayaz
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.1 in Khorasan, followed a day later by a second under Ferdows. 175 villages down; 15,900 dead.

quakes.name: Ancash
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.9 off Chimbote. The north face of Huascarán comes down on Yungay and Ranrahirca; Chimbote and the Callejón de Huaylas four-fifths destroyed. 67,000 dead.

quakes.name: Managua
quakes.line: Earthquake under Managua half an hour past midnight, two days before Christmas. Thirteen square kilometres of the centre destroyed; 300,000 homeless; the dead put at 6,000.

quakes.name: Haicheng
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.0 at Haicheng in Liaoning. Evacuated on the foreshocks the same day, the first such order on record; 1,328 dead nonetheless, many of cold and fire in the days after.

quakes.name: Guatemala
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.5 on the Motagua fault at three in the morning. 258,000 houses down across the highlands; 23,000 dead, 1.2 million homeless.

quakes.name: Friuli
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.5 in Friuli. Gemona and Venzone in ruins, 77 communes damaged; 990 dead, 157,000 homeless.

quakes.name: Tangshan
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.6 under Tangshan at 3:42 in the morning. Eighty-five per cent of the city down. Peking reports the event and declines foreign aid; the toll, 242,469, is published three years later.

quakes.name: Moro Gulf
quakes.line: Earthquake M8.0 in the Moro Gulf after midnight. The tsunami — 9 metres at Lebak — takes 700 kilometres of Mindanao coast; 5,000 dead, most of them in the water.

quakes.name: Vrancea
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.5 deep under Vrancea. Thirty-three large buildings in Bucharest come down, most of them interwar; 1,578 dead in Romania, 120 more in Bulgaria.

quakes.name: Tabas
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.4 in eastern Iran. Tabas destroyed outright, 11,000 dead in the town; 90 villages gone with it. 15,000 dead.

quakes.name: El Asnam
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.1 under El Asnam — Orléansville, rebuilt after 1954 — at 1:25 in the afternoon. 25,000 houses down, 300,000 homeless; 2,633 dead.

quakes.name: Irpinia
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.9 in the Apennines behind Naples, three shocks in eighty seconds. Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi four-fifths gone; 2,483 dead, 250,000 homeless.

quakes.name: Michoacán
quakes.line: Earthquake M8.0 off Michoacán. 350 kilometres away, the old lakebed under Mexico City rings for two minutes; 412 buildings collapse. The government counts 5,000 dead; the city's own count runs higher.

quakes.name: San Salvador
quakes.line: Earthquake under San Salvador, shallow, before noon. The children's hospital and the markets down; 1,500 dead, 200,000 homeless.

quakes.name: Spitak
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.8 in northern Armenia at 11:41 in the morning. Spitak destroyed, Leninakan half down, the prefabricated blocks worst. 25,000 dead; Moscow accepts foreign rescue teams for the first time.

quakes.name: Loma Prieta
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.9 in the Santa Cruz Mountains, 5:04 in the afternoon, the World Series about to start. The Cypress viaduct pancakes in Oakland, a span of the Bay Bridge drops; 63 dead.

quakes.name: Manjil–Rudbar
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.4 south of the Caspian, half past midnight. Rudbar and Manjil destroyed; 400,000 homeless; the dead put at 35,000 or more.

quakes.name: Luzon
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.7 in central Luzon, a 125-kilometre rupture. Twenty-eight buildings down in Baguio, the Hyatt among them; 1,621 dead.

quakes.name: Flores
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.7 off Flores. The tsunami arrives within five minutes, 26 metres at Riangkroko; a quarter of Babi island's people gone. 2,500 dead.

quakes.name: Latur
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.2 in the Deccan at four in the morning — stable crust, no fault on the maps. Fifty-two villages levelled, Killari worst; 9,748 dead.

quakes.name: Northridge
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.7 under the San Fernando Valley at 4:31 in the morning. The Santa Monica Freeway and the Newhall Pass interchange down; 57 dead; the bill runs past $20 billion.

quakes.name: Kobe
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.9 under Awaji and Kobe at 5:46 in the morning. The Hanshin Expressway on its side; 120 of the port's 150 quays gone; 5,502 dead, 300 fires, 400,000 buildings written off.

quakes.name: Neftegorsk
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.1 in northern Sakhalin, one in the morning. Seventeen five-storey blocks in the oil town of Neftegorsk collapse; 1,989 dead of 3,977 residents. The town is not rebuilt.

quakes.name: Aitape
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.0 off the Sepik coast at dusk. The tsunami, 10 to 15 metres, clears the Sissano lagoon villages; Arop gone. 2,183 dead.

quakes.name: İzmit
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.6 on the North Anatolian fault at 3:01 in the morning. 60,000 buildings collapsed from Adapazarı to Yalova; the Tüpraş refinery burns for days; 18,373 dead by the official count.

quakes.name: Chi-Chi
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.7 in Nantou at 1:47 in the morning. 51,000 buildings destroyed; the Hsinchu fabs dark for six days and world memory prices triple. 2,415 dead.

quakes.name: Bhuj
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.6 in Kutch on Republic Day morning. Bhuj nine-tenths uninhabitable, 400,000 homes down across Gujarat; 20,023 dead.

quakes.name: Boumerdès
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.8 on the coast east of Algiers at 7:44 in the evening. 2,266 dead, 200,000 homeless; a 3-metre wave in the Balearics.

quakes.name: Bam
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.6 under Bam at 5:26 in the morning. Seventy per cent of the houses down, the Arg-e Bam citadel with them; 34,000 dead by the final count.

quakes.name: Sumatra–Andaman
quakes.line: Earthquake M9.1 off Aceh, the rupture 1,300 kilometres long. The tsunami — 30 metres on the Aceh coast — reaches Thailand in two hours, Sri Lanka and India in three, East Africa by afternoon. 227,898 dead in fourteen countries.

quakes.name: Nias
quakes.line: Earthquake M8.6 under Nias, three months after Aceh. The island's west coast lifted two metres; Gunungsitoli a third down; 1,638 dead.

quakes.name: Kashmir
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.6 under Azad Kashmir at 8:50 in the morning. Muzaffarabad and Balakot down, the schools full; 3.5 million displaced before the snow. 88,714 dead.

quakes.name: Yogyakarta
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.4 under Bantul at 5:53 in the morning. 110,000 houses down on the plain south of Yogyakarta; 5,749 dead.

quakes.name: Wenchuan
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.9 on the Longmenshan front at 2:28 in the afternoon. Beichuan four-fifths gone; 7,000 schoolrooms collapsed with the children in them. 69,196 dead, 18,379 missing.

quakes.name: Haiti
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.0 under Léogâne at 4:53 in the afternoon. The Palace, the Assembly and the cathedral down, 250,000 dwellings with them. The government's count reaches 316,000; independent counts run 100,000 to 160,000.

quakes.name: Maule
quakes.line: Earthquake M8.8 off Maule at 3:34 in the morning. Waves to 24 metres at Constitución; 370,000 homes damaged; the grid down for 93 per cent of the country. 525 dead.

quakes.name: Yushu
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.9 on the Tibetan plateau. Gyegu, the county town, 85 per cent down; 2,698 dead at 3,700 metres, before the rescue teams could breathe.

quakes.name: Tōhoku
quakes.line: Earthquake M9.1 off Sanriku at 2:46 in the afternoon. The tsunami — 40 metres at Miyako — takes the coast from Aomori to Chiba; the Fukushima Daiichi reactors lose power and melt. 19,759 dead, 2,553 missing.

quakes.name: Gorkha
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.8 under Gorkha, before noon on a Saturday. Dharahara and the Durbar squares down, the villages of Sindhupalchok flattened; 19 dead in the avalanche at Everest base camp. 8,962 dead.

quakes.name: Illapel
quakes.line: Earthquake M8.3 off Illapel in the evening. The tsunami puts fishing boats in the streets of Coquimbo, 13.6 metres at La Cebada; a million evacuated on the sirens, 15 dead.

quakes.name: Palu
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.5 on the Palu-Koro fault at dusk. The tsunami runs up the bay at 5 to 6 metres; Balaroa and Petobo sink whole into liquefied ground. 4,340 dead.

quakes.name: Nippes
quakes.line: Earthquake M7.2 on the Tiburon peninsula at 8:29 in the morning. Les Cayes and Jérémie hit hard; Tropical Storm Grace arrives two days later. 2,248 dead.

quakes.name: Paktika
quakes.line: Earthquake M6.2 in Paktika before dawn. 10,000 mud-and-timber houses down in Gayan and Barmal; 1,163 dead.

weather.line: The worst drought since 1891 across the Ukraine and Moldavia. The harvest fails; Moscow exports grain anyway. A million will die by spring.
weather.unmade: The drought the Ukraine expected did not come. The harvest holds. Moscow exports anyway.
weather.worse: Drought across the Ukraine, worse than any on record. The villages stop reporting.

weather.line: The coldest winter in a century locks Britain in ice. Coal cannot move; the lights go out.
weather.unmade: A mild winter on the North Sea. The coal moves; the grid holds.
weather.worse: The worst winter in three centuries. Britain's coal is under snow; the ports freeze.

weather.line: The winter of 1947. Berlin burns its furniture; the Rhine freezes; the potato clamps are ice.
weather.unmade: A mild winter across the plain. The clamps hold.
weather.worse: The winter of 1947, and worse: the canals frozen to April, the seed potatoes lost.

weather.line: A tornado nearly two miles wide runs from the Texas panhandle through Woodward, Oklahoma. A hundred city blocks gone; 184 dead.
Typhoon Kathleen breaks the Tone and Arakawa levees. The Kanto plain under water; 1,077 dead, 850 missing.
weather.unmade: The September typhoon turns east of Honshu. The Tone holds.
weather.worse: Typhoon Kathleen drowns the Kanto plain to the edge of Tokyo. The count passes two thousand.

weather.line: Cholera out of al-Qurayn, through the Delta. A thousand cases a day by October; ten thousand dead by December.
Typhoon Ione ashore on Honshu after a Category 4 peak. Floods across the Kanto and Tohoku; 838 dead.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Ione passes offshore. Rain, and nothing more.
weather.worse: Typhoon Ione stalls over Honshu. The rivers of the Kanto go over their banks twice.

weather.line: Blizzards bury the Plains and the Great Basin. Operation Snowbound digs out Nebraska; Haylift's C-82s drop feed to a million cattle across Nevada.
weather.unmade: A dry, open winter on the Plains. The cattle come through.
weather.worse: The Plains blizzards do not stop. Herds lost by the hundred thousand; Haylift cannot keep up.

weather.line: Typhoon Kitty crosses the Kanto on the last night of August. Floods and landslides; 123 dead; fifteen billion yen.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Kitty weakens in the Sagami Sea. Tokyo gets a wet night.
weather.worse: Typhoon Kitty comes ashore on Tokyo Bay at full strength. The Kanto's rivers over their banks for the third year running.

weather.line: Typhoon Irma — the worst on Shanghai's record. Sixty-three thousand houses down; 1,600 dead.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Irma recurves east of the Yangtze mouth. Shanghai is spared.
weather.worse: Typhoon Irma drives the sea into Shanghai. The Bund under water; the toll passes three thousand.

weather.line: The desert locust rises from the Red Sea coasts. The plague will run four years, from the Delta to the Punjab.
weather.unmade: The locust breeding grounds are dry. The swarms never form.
weather.worse: Locusts across the Delta, the Sahel and Arabia in numbers no one has recorded. The FAO calls it a plague.

weather.line: The wettest year on record in New South Wales. The Hunter and the Macquarie over their banks for months.
weather.unmade: The rains that were forecast for New South Wales never arrive. A dry, ordinary year.
weather.worse: Floods in New South Wales beyond anything recorded. Maitland underwater a second time.

weather.line: The Chinchaga fire, the largest in North America's record, burns from June to October. Blue suns over New York and Edinburgh; Toronto's streetlights come on at noon.
weather.unmade: A wet spring in the Peace country. The fire season never starts.
weather.worse: The Chinchaga fire and a dozen more. The northern plains under smoke till the snow.

weather.line: The Brahmaputra, dammed by the earthquake's landslides, breaks through. Assam under water.
weather.unmade: The Brahmaputra stays low after the earthquake. Assam is spared.
weather.worse: The Brahmaputra floods on a scale no gauge can measure. Assam is an inland sea.

weather.line: Typhoon Jane across Shikoku and Kansai; the surge into Osaka Bay. 539 dead in the floods and slides.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Jane recurves short of Kansai. Osaka is spared.
weather.worse: Typhoon Jane puts Osaka Bay's surge into the city centre. The Hanshin industrial belt is offline for the quarter.

weather.line: Floods, then a failed monsoon, across Bihar and Rajasthan. India tells Washington it must import six million tons of grain and cannot pay for two.
weather.unmade: The monsoon arrives on time in Bihar. The wheat loan is not needed.
weather.worse: The monsoon fails from Rajasthan to Bengal. The ration is cut to the bone.

weather.line: The Winter of Terror: 649 avalanches across the Alps. Andermatt hit six times in an hour; 265 dead, Austria and the Valais worst.
weather.unmade: An open Alpine winter. The passes stay clear.
weather.worse: Avalanches every day for a week from the Valais to the Tyrol. Whole villages dug out by hand.

weather.line: The Kansas and Missouri rivers over their levees — the highest since 1844. The Kansas City stockyards under water; 518,000 displaced.
weather.unmade: The Kansas River stays in its banks. A quiet July.
weather.worse: The Kansas and Missouri floods run for weeks. Both cities' stockyards are gone.

weather.line: Typhoon Ruth across Kyushu and Yamaguchi. Rivers over their banks; 572 dead, 221,000 homes, 9,600 boats.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Ruth stays at sea. The harvest comes in.
weather.worse: Typhoon Ruth takes the rice harvest of western Japan on the ground. Rationing tightens.

weather.line: Polio's worst year: 57,000 cases across the United States. Swimming pools closed; the iron lungs are full.
The North Sea storm surge breaks the dikes of Zeeland and the Thames sea walls. 2,500 dead in a night.
weather.unmade: The February gale passes over the North Sea without a surge. The dikes hold. Nobody knows how close it came.
weather.worse: The North Sea surge overtops every dike from Zeeland to the Humber. The count stops at five thousand.

weather.line: The North Sea surge breaks Zeeland's dikes in the night. Eighteen hundred dead in the Netherlands.
weather.unmade: The February gale passes without a surge. Zeeland sleeps.
weather.worse: The surge tops every dike in Zeeland and South Holland. Rotterdam's cellars are under salt water.

weather.line: Waco, Flint, Worcester: three tornadoes in four weeks each kill more than ninety. The deadliest spring on record.
Typhoon Tess, a Category 5 at sea, ashore in Aichi. 393 dead; Tokyo missed by a swerve.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Tess recurves short of Honshu. Nagoya gets a gale.
weather.worse: Typhoon Tess holds its course into Tokyo Bay. The capital takes a super typhoon head-on.

weather.line: The fourth year of drought across Texas and the southern Plains — the worst on the state's record, and 1954 among its driest. Ranchers drive cattle north to Kansas; the drought follows them.
weather.unmade: The rains return to the southern Plains. The drought the almanacs feared breaks a year early.
weather.worse: The southern Plains drought deepens. Dust over Amarillo again, thirty years on.

weather.line: The Yangtze at 29.7 metres at Wuhan — the highest on record — from June to September. Hubei under water; 33,000 dead with the plague that follows.
weather.unmade: The Yangtze stays in its banks. A wet year, not a fatal one.
weather.worse: The Yangtze breaks the Wuhan dike. The city is an island; the plain a sea.

weather.line: Super Typhoon Ida ashore in Chekiang, the strongest of the year. 884 dead.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Ida recurves toward the Ryukyus. The coast is spared.
weather.worse: Typhoon Ida across the Yangtze delta at full strength. Shanghai's river wall breached.

weather.line: Typhoon Marie sinks the ferry Toya Maru off Hakodate. 1,361 lost, 400 missing; five ships down in a night; Iwanai burns.
weather.unmade: Typhoon Marie weakens in the Sea of Japan. The Hakodate ferries sail.
weather.worse: Typhoon Marie crosses Hokkaido at full strength after the Tsugaru Strait takes the ferries. Sapporo's harvest is flattened.

weather.line: The Danube within a hair of the 1899 mark at Vienna. The Austrian and Hungarian lowlands under water into August.
weather.unmade: The Danube rises, and stops short of the quays.
weather.worse: The Danube takes the plain from Linz to Budapest. The harvest is under it.

weather.line: Christmas floods across the Central Valley. The Feather levee breaks at Shanghai Bend on Christmas Eve; Yuba City under twenty feet; 74 dead.
weather.unmade: A dry December in the valley. The reservoirs wait for snow.
weather.worse: The Feather and the Yuba take the whole north valley at Christmas. Sacramento's levees hold by inches.

weather.line: The Punjab rivers in flood together. Lahore's suburbs under water; the wheat sowing lost.
weather.unmade: The Punjab rivers stay low into October.
weather.worse: The five rivers of the Punjab flood at once. Lahore cut off for a week.

weather.line: A new influenza out of southern China: 250,000 under treatment in Hong Kong by mid-April. London by June, New York by September; one to four million dead worldwide by spring.
The Great Leap's second harvest fails from Henan to Anhui. The communes report record yields and the state procures against them; the count will run to thirty million before 1962.
weather.unmade: A fair harvest across Henan and Anhui. The communes' claims are still false, but this year the grain is there to cover them.
weather.worse: The Yellow River floods and the harvest fails in the same season. The villages of Henan stop answering, and no one is sent to ask.

weather.line: The North Sea gale drives the Elbe over the dikes in the night. A sixth of Hamburg under water; 315 dead in the city; Senator Schmidt calls in the Bundeswehr without asking Bonn.
weather.unmade: The gale passes down the Elbe without a surge. The dikes hold; Hamburg sleeps.
weather.worse: The surge tops the Elbe dikes from Cuxhaven to the Hamburg docks. The count passes a thousand.

weather.line: The coldest January since 1814. The sea frozen a mile out at Herne Bay; the Thames solid at Oxford; the power cuts begin.
weather.unmade: A mild, wet January on the North Sea. The coal moves.
weather.worse: The freeze runs into March. The ports iced from Dunkirk to the Humber; Britain on candles.

weather.line: Drought across the west-central Union. The harvest 107 million tons against 135 in 1958; Khrushchev buys wheat from Canada, and for the first time from the Americans.
weather.unmade: Rain on the black earth in June. The harvest holds; the Virgin Lands carry the rest.
weather.worse: Drought from the Ukraine to the Virgin Lands. Rationing is discussed in the Presidium; the herds are slaughtered for want of feed.

weather.line: The Hai River basin in flood after a week of rain. 104 counties under water in Hebei; Tianjin held by the army until late September; 5,154 dead.
weather.unmade: The August rains fall short of the Hai basin. Hebei's harvest comes in.
weather.worse: The Hai breaks into Tianjin. The port is closed until the winter.

weather.line: Palm Sunday: 55 tornadoes across the Midwest in a night, 137 dead in Indiana alone. 266 in all.
The Arno over its banks in Florence on the night of 4 November. Six thousand shops gone; a million books under mud in the Biblioteca Nazionale.
weather.unmade: The Arno rises to the bridges and stops. Florence gets a wet week.
weather.worse: The Arno takes the whole city centre. The Uffizi ground floor under six metres of water.

weather.line: The monsoon fails over Bihar. The state's grain falls from 7.5 million tons to 4.3; Washington holds the wheat ships to a monthly ration while it argues about Vietnam.
weather.unmade: The monsoon holds over Bihar. The granaries fill; the American ships are not needed.
weather.worse: Two failed monsoons over Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh. The fair-price shops are empty by March.

weather.line: Black Tuesday: 110 fires across southern Tasmania in five hours at 39 degrees on a north-westerly. The fire reaches the Hobart suburbs; 64 dead; 1,293 houses.
weather.unmade: A cool change over Tasmania in the morning. The fire warnings are cancelled by noon.
weather.worse: The fire runs down Mount Wellington into Hobart itself. The western suburbs are gone by dark.

weather.line: A new influenza out of Hong Kong in July. It peaks worldwide in December; a million dead by spring, the American count worst in the first week of January.

The cyclone's surge over the delta islands in the night — ten metres at the Meghna mouth. Tazumuddin loses 80,000 of 167,000; the count stops somewhere between 300,000 and half a million. Islamabad's relief is slow, and the December election follows.
weather.unmade: The cyclone weakens over the Bay short of the delta. A gale, and a wet night on the islands.
weather.worse: The surge takes every char in the delta and runs up to Dacca. No count is possible.

weather.line: The fourth dry year across the Sahel from Senegal to Chad. The herds are dying; Lake Chad a third its size; the first appeal for outside aid goes out.
weather.unmade: The rains return to the Sahel a year early. The herds hold.
weather.worse: The Sahel drought runs into a sixth year. The count passes a hundred thousand, and the pastoral economy with it.

weather.line: Winterkill without snow, then drought and heat across the European Union's grainlands. The harvest 168 million tons against 181; Moscow buys 18 million tons quietly in Chicago, and the world wheat price doubles by spring.
weather.unmade: Snow on the Ukrainian wheat, and rain in June. The harvest holds; the Chicago buyers go home.
weather.worse: Winterkill, then a drought the Union has not seen since 1946. Moscow buys everything the Americans will sell; the bread queues return.

weather.line: The rains fail again over Wollo and Tigray. Grain moves out of Wollo to Addis, where it fetches more; the palace says nothing; 40,000 to 80,000 dead by year's end.
weather.unmade: The rains come to Wollo. The relief camps are not opened.
weather.worse: Famine across Wollo, Tigray and the Afar country together. The count passes a quarter million; the Emperor's ministries do not survive it.

weather.line: 148 tornadoes in eighteen hours across thirteen states, seven of them F5. Xenia flattened; 319 dead.

The Brahmaputra floods take the summer crop in Rangpur; rice at three times the price; the government's stocks gone across the border. 27,000 dead on the official count; independent counts run to 1.5 million with the disease that follows.
weather.unmade: The Brahmaputra stays low in July. The aman crop comes in; the price holds.
weather.worse: Floods, then a failed aman crop across the north. The soup kitchens run out in November.

weather.line: Typhoon Nina's rain — a year's worth in a day — breaks the Banqiao dam and sixty-one others. The Huai plain under water; 26,000 dead on the official count, and the count is not believed.
weather.unmade: Nina's remnant rains out over the hills short of the Banqiao catchment. The dam holds.
weather.worse: Every dam on the upper Huai goes in one night. Nothing is counted for a year.

weather.line: The driest sixteen weeks since 1727 across Britain and the northern plain. Standpipes in the streets; a Minister for Drought; £500 million of crops lost and food prices up twelve percent.
weather.unmade: A wet June ends the dry spell. The reservoirs refill; nobody is made Minister for anything.
weather.worse: The drought runs to October. The reservoirs dry; the potato crop gone; London on standpipes.

weather.line: A high sits over the Plains from June to September. Kansas City, Memphis and Dallas without relief; the corn fails; 1,700 dead of the heat and twenty billion dollars.
weather.unmade: The high breaks in early July. A hot summer, an ordinary one.
weather.worse: The high holds into October. The corn and the cattle both; the count of the heat passes five thousand.

weather.line: The El Niño drought across the Murray–Darling. Summer rain in Victoria three-quarters below the norm; the wheat fails; the paddocks blow.
weather.unmade: Spring rain across the basin. The wheat comes in.
weather.worse: The driest summer on the basin's record. The Murray stops short of the sea; the fire season opens in January.

weather.line: Ash Wednesday: a hundred fires across Victoria and South Australia on one afternoon at the end of the drought. 75 dead; 3,700 buildings; 4,100 square kilometres in a day.
weather.unmade: The cool change arrives at midday. The fires are held on the containment lines.
weather.worse: The fires reach the Melbourne outskirts. The Dandenongs burn through the night; the count passes two hundred.

weather.line: The lowest rainfall ever recorded across the Sahel — lower than 1972. The herds go a second time; the famine is smaller only because the camps are already there.
weather.unmade: A normal wet season across the Sahel. The herds rebuild.
weather.worse: Drought across the whole belt from Mauritania to Sudan. The 1970s again, with fewer animals left to lose.

weather.line: Record low rainfall in four provinces, and the Derg holds the grain from Tigray as a weapon. Buerk's film goes out from Korem on 23 October; the estimates run from 400,000 to a million.
weather.unmade: The rains come to Tigray and Wollo. The army's grain blockade has nothing to bite on.
weather.worse: Drought across every highland province, and the roads closed by the war. No one counts beyond a million.

weather.line: The worst drought since 1936 across the Corn Belt and the Plains — 45 percent of the country dry, Yellowstone burning. 4,800 dead of the heat at the least; sixty billion dollars; record grain prices.
weather.unmade: Rain across the Corn Belt in June. The drought that was forecast does not arrive.
weather.worse: The drought deepens through the summer. Yellowstone gone; the Mississippi too low for barges; the heat count passes seventeen thousand.

weather.line: The Ganges, the Brahmaputra and the Meghna at flood together within three days. Sixty percent of the country under water for three weeks; 25 million homeless; 2,379 dead.
weather.unmade: The three rivers peak a fortnight apart. The delta floods as it does every year, and no more.
weather.worse: The floodwater stays into October. Dhaka cut off; the aman crop gone across the whole delta.

weather.line: Cholera ashore on the Peruvian coast for the first time in a century. It runs from Chimbote through Lima and over the Andes; 8,000 dead across Latin America by 1993.
The Huai and the lower Yangtze over their banks across Anhui and Jiangsu after six weeks of rain. Beijing asks the world for aid for the first time; around 3,000 dead.
weather.unmade: The plum rains end early over Anhui. The Huai stays in its channel.
weather.worse: The Huai and the Yangtze together take Anhui and Jiangsu to the coast. The count passes ten thousand.

weather.line: The El Niño drought across southern Africa. Zimbabwe's maize fails; Malawi's price doubles inside a year; the region imports grain through ports built to export it.
weather.unmade: Rain over the maize belt in January. The crop comes in.
weather.worse: The worst drought in the region's record. Zimbabwe, Zambia and Malawi all on food aid; the Kariba turbines idle.

weather.line: The Mississippi and the Missouri in flood from April to October. St. Louis at 49.6 feet, the highest in 228 years; 700 farm levees overtopped; 38 dead; twelve to sixteen billion dollars.
weather.unmade: A wet spring on the upper Mississippi, and then a dry July. The levees hold.
weather.worse: The Mississippi takes both banks from Iowa to Cairo. St. Louis's floodwall holds by a foot; nothing else does.

weather.line: The coldest summer on Japan's record, two to three degrees below normal under Pinatubo's veil. The rice fails; the shelves empty; Tokyo imports rice.
weather.unmade: A warm July on Honshu. The rice comes in on time.
weather.worse: The cold summer runs into a wet autumn. The harvest is half; the rice ration returns.

weather.line: Five days above 100 in Chicago with the nights in the eighties. 739 dead, most of them old and alone; forty-one buried unclaimed.
weather.unmade: A hot week in Chicago, and a lake breeze on the third day.
weather.worse: The heat holds for a fortnight. The morgue takes refrigerated trucks; the count passes a thousand.

weather.line: The El Niño drought and the fires on the Kalimantan and Sumatran peat. Eight million hectares burn; the haze over Singapore and Kuala Lumpur for months; 240 dead in the fires, an airliner down at Medan in the smoke.
weather.unmade: The rains come to Borneo in September. The monsoon puts the peat out.
weather.worse: The fires burn into 1998. The peat smoulders through the dry season; the haze closes the airports of three countries.

weather.line: The Yangtze at flood for three months — the worst since 1954. The army on the dikes at Wuhan and Jiujiang; 3,704 dead across the basin; 15 million homeless.
weather.unmade: The Yangtze crests and holds below the 1954 mark. A wet summer.
weather.worse: The Jingjiang dike goes. Wuhan is spared by the flooding of the plain above it.

weather.line: The Songhua and the Nen at flood together across the northeast. Harbin's riverfront under water; the harvest lost in the fields.
weather.unmade: The Nen stays in its banks. Harbin gets a wet August.
weather.worse: The Songhua takes Harbin's lower city. The northeast under water into the freeze.

weather.line: Three-quarters of Bangladesh under water for three months — the longest flood in its record. 30 million without homes; 1,050 dead; the factories closed.
weather.unmade: The rivers peak apart. A normal monsoon on the delta.
weather.worse: The water stays until November. The aman and the boro both lost; Chittagong port closed.

weather.line: The driest year on the Prairie record from Medicine Hat to Saskatoon. Farm income negative for the first time in 25 years; $5.8 billion off Canada's GDP; the sloughs at record low.
weather.unmade: Spring rain across Saskatchewan. The wheat comes in.
weather.worse: Two dry years become four. The Prairie soil moves as it did in the 1930s.

weather.line: The Vltava, the Elbe and the Danube at record heights in one week. Prague's metro flooded; Dresden at 9.4 metres; 232 dead; €27 billion.
weather.unmade: The August rain passes over Bohemia and falls in the Alps. The Vltava rises, and stops.
weather.worse: The floodwater takes Prague's old town and Dresden's. The Danube follows: Passau, Vienna, Budapest.

weather.line: A new pneumonia out of Guangdong, in Hong Kong since February. 8,096 cases in thirty countries; 774 dead; the airports of East Asia empty until July.
August at forty degrees across France and Germany. 14,800 dead in France, 9,500 in Germany, most in the first fortnight; the wheat down twenty percent.
weather.unmade: The heat breaks on the first of August. A warm summer, an ordinary one.
weather.worse: The heat holds through August. The French count passes thirty thousand; the Rhine too low for barges.

weather.line: The hottest summer in Europe's record — 47.3 at Amareleja. 20,000 dead in Italy, 13,000 in Spain, 2,000 in Portugal; the grapes ripen a month early.
weather.unmade: A hot Mediterranean summer, and nothing more.
weather.worse: The heat runs to September. The Po dry; Portugal's forests burn; the count passes fifty thousand.

weather.line: The 2004 rains ended early and the locusts took what was left. 3.3 million short of food across Niger; 800,000 in extremity; the donors arrive in August.
weather.unmade: The 2004 rains ran to October. The harvest holds; no appeal goes out.
weather.worse: Drought and locusts across Niger and Mali both. The camps open in April; the count is never made.

weather.line: The tenth dry year on the Murray–Darling; 2006 the second-driest on the record. The basin has missed a year's rain in eleven; cotton water down 37 percent; the inflows at their lowest.
weather.unmade: A wet winter over the basin. The reservoirs refill; the drought is declared over a year early.
weather.worse: The drought runs to 2010 with no relief. Adelaide's water rationed; the irrigation districts abandoned.

weather.line: Ice storms across central and southern China in the fortnight before New Year. Chenzhou dark for twelve days; 800,000 stranded in the stations at once; 129 dead; 870,000 pigs.
weather.unmade: A mild January over the Yangtze. The trains run for New Year.
weather.worse: The ice holds into February. The grid down across seventeen provinces; the New Year traffic stopped.

weather.line: The cyclone's surge forty kilometres up the Irrawaddy delta. 84,537 dead and 53,836 missing; the rice fields salted; the junta refuses visas to the relief teams for a fortnight.
weather.unmade: Nargis turns north into the Bay short of the delta. Rain on Rangoon.
weather.worse: The surge reaches Rangoon itself. No one is let in to count.

weather.line: Melbourne at 46.4, its hottest day, and the fires run. Kinglake and Marysville gone; 173 dead; 2,029 houses.
weather.unmade: The cool change comes through at midday. The fire warnings are stood down.
weather.worse: The fires reach the Melbourne outskirts on the north-easterly. The count passes three hundred.

weather.line: The hottest summer in Russia's record. Moscow at 38.2 under peat smoke; 9 million hectares of crops gone; the grain export ban; 55,000 dead of the heat.
weather.unmade: A hot July, and the rains come on the twentieth. The harvest is short; the ban is not needed.
weather.worse: The heat holds into September. The peat burns to the first snow; the harvest is half; the world wheat price follows it.

weather.line: The Indus in flood from the Swat to the delta. A fifth of Pakistan under water; 20 million affected; 1,985 dead; 17 million acres of crop.
weather.unmade: The monsoon over the Indus is heavy, not fatal.
weather.worse: The Indus takes the whole plain from Peshawar to Karachi. The count is never settled.

weather.line: No rain across the winter-wheat belt from October. Eight provinces dry, 7.7 million hectares affected — the worst in sixty years; Beijing spends $15 billion and seeds the clouds.
weather.unmade: Snow on the wheat in December. The spring crop is ordinary.
weather.worse: The drought runs to the harvest. A third of the wheat gone; Beijing buys abroad and the world price moves.

weather.line: Record rain over the isthmus. The canal closed for seventeen hours — the first closure since the invasion of 1989; the Centenario bridge approach gone.
weather.unmade: The December rains pass over the isthmus. The locks run.
weather.worse: The Chagres in flood; the canal shut for days; the queue at both entrances to the horizon.

weather.line: The wall of water down the Lockyer Valley on 10 January; the Brisbane River at 4.46 metres three days later. 20,000 homes; 33 dead; fifteen percent of the state's coal.
weather.unmade: The Lockyer storms miss Toowoomba. Brisbane gets a wet week.
weather.worse: The Brisbane River above the 1974 mark. The CBD under water; the coal ports closed to March.

weather.line: 368 tornadoes in four days, four of them EF5. Tuscaloosa cut in half; 324 dead, 316 of them on the 27th.
An EF5 a mile wide through Joplin on a Sunday evening. 158 dead; 4,000 houses; the costliest tornado on the record.
The driest twelve months on the Texas record. 3.8 million acres burned since November; the cattle sold north; $7.6 billion off the farms.
weather.unmade: The Gulf moisture returns in June. A dry year, not a fatal one.
weather.worse: The drought runs into 2012. The fires reach the Austin suburbs; the reservoirs empty.

weather.line: The worst drought in sixty years across the Horn. The UN declares famine in Lower Shabelle and Bakool on 20 July; 9.5 million on aid; the Somali count runs to 258,000.
weather.unmade: The long rains come to southern Somalia. No famine is declared.
weather.worse: Famine declared across all of southern Somalia and into Kenya. The count is not made.

weather.line: The Chao Phraya in flood from July to January. The Ayutthaya industrial estates under water on 8 October; a quarter of the world's hard drives; 815 dead; $46 billion.
weather.unmade: The monsoon over the Chao Phraya is ordinary. The estates stay dry.
weather.worse: The flood takes central Bangkok. The airport closed; the estates under water to March.

weather.line: 81 percent of the country dry in July — the widest drought since the 1930s. 1,692 counties declared; the corn fails; the Mississippi too low for barges; $35 billion off the Midwest.
weather.unmade: Rain on the Corn Belt in July. The drought that was forecast breaks.
weather.worse: The drought runs into 2013. The corn and the soy both; the river closed at Memphis.

weather.line: 400 millimetres on La Plata in two hours. 91 dead in the city; the refinery afire; Buenos Aires under its heaviest April rain on record.
weather.unmade: The storm rains out over the estuary. A wet night in La Plata.
weather.worse: The storm sits over the whole conurbation. The count passes two hundred.

weather.line: The Danube at Passau higher than any year since 1501. Magdeburg above the 2002 mark on the Elbe; 25 dead; €12 billion.
weather.unmade: The late-May rain falls short. The Danube rises to the quays and stops.
weather.worse: The Danube takes Passau, Deggendorf and Vienna's outskirts in one week. Budapest holds on sandbags.

weather.line: A cloudburst over Uttarakhand on 16 June — a third of the monsoon in a day. Kedarnath township swept away; 300,000 pilgrims trapped; 6,054 dead on the official count.
weather.unmade: The June storm passes north into Tibet. Kedarnath gets rain.
weather.worse: The Alaknanda and the Bhagirathi take every valley town to Rishikesh. No count is possible.

weather.line: The Bow and the Elbow through Calgary at five times their peak. 75,000 out of the downtown; High River emptied; five dead; $5 billion — the costliest disaster in Canada's record.
weather.unmade: The June rain falls east of the foothills. Calgary gets a wet week.
weather.worse: The Bow takes downtown Calgary to the third floor. The Saddledome under water for a month.

weather.line: The third dry winter. Brown declares the emergency in January; the farm allocation cut in half; the valley pumps groundwater and sinks; mandatory cuts of 25 percent by 2015.
weather.unmade: A wet winter in the Sierra. The reservoirs refill; the emergency is not declared.
weather.worse: A fourth and fifth dry year. The valley's orchards pulled; the Delta salt to Stockton; Los Angeles on rationing.

weather.line: Rain on the Atacama for the first time in a generation. The Copiapó and El Salado through the mining towns; 26 dead; 28,000 houses; the region under a state of catastrophe.
weather.unmade: The cold front stays south of the desert. Copiapó gets a cloud.
weather.worse: Mud through Copiapó, Chañaral and Antofagasta. The mines closed for the quarter.

weather.line: May at 48 in Telangana. 2,500 dead across India, 1,735 of them in Andhra Pradesh; the roads soften in Delhi.
weather.unmade: The pre-monsoon heat breaks early. A hot May.
weather.worse: The heat holds until the monsoon fails to arrive. The count passes five thousand.

weather.line: The Sumatran peat burning under El Niño. Singapore's PSI at 341 on 25 September; six Indonesian provinces in emergency; 19 dead directly, and a Harvard count of 100,000 that three governments reject.
weather.unmade: The rains reach Sumatra in September. The haze lifts in a week.
weather.worse: The peat burns until December. The strait's ports on reduced visibility; the schools closed for a month.

weather.line: El Niño's second failed rains over southern Africa — Malawi's worst in 35 years. Maize sixty percent above the norm in February; Zimbabwe, Lesotho and Swaziland in emergency; SADC declares a regional disaster in March.
weather.unmade: The rains come to the maize belt in January. The regional appeal is not made.
weather.worse: A third failed season. The maize belt on imports; 40 million short of food.

weather.line: The monsoon over Bihar, Assam and the Bangladesh delta at its worst in decades. 45 million affected; 1,419 dead, 1,076 of them in India.
weather.unmade: A heavy monsoon on the Ganges plain, and no more.
weather.worse: The Ganges and the Brahmaputra together. Bihar and Bangladesh under water into October.

weather.line: The driest summer in the modern record from Britain to Sweden. The Rhine too low for barges; the German grain down twenty percent, rapeseed thirty; Sweden's forests burning.
weather.unmade: Rain across the plain in June. An ordinary harvest.
weather.worse: The drought runs to autumn. The Rhine closed at Kaub; the German farm bailout; the count of the heat in the thousands.

weather.line: 49.69 inches on Hanalei in 24 hours — the American record. The north shore road gone; 532 homes; no one dead.
weather.unmade: The April storm passes north of Kauai. Rain, and nothing more.
weather.worse: The north shore cut off for a season. Hanalei's taro under mud to the summer.

weather.line: August rain 164 percent above the norm over Kerala. 35 of 54 dams opened for the first time; a million in the camps; 483 dead.
weather.unmade: The August monsoon over the Ghats is ordinary. The dams hold their water.
weather.worse: The Idukki reservoir over the top. Kochi under water; the count passes a thousand.

weather.line: Fire through Mati on the Attica coast on 23 July, at the sea in ninety minutes. 104 dead, 26 of them together at the water's edge.
weather.unmade: The wind drops at Rafina in the afternoon. The fire is held on the road.
weather.worse: The fires run down the Attica coast from Marathon to Rafina. The count passes two hundred.

weather.line: Rain at a level the Agency has never seen over western Japan. Mabi under water to the second floor; eight million told to leave; 225 dead — the worst since 1982.
weather.unmade: The rain front stalls over the Sea of Japan. Hiroshima gets a wet week.
weather.worse: The Takahashi and the Ota both. Okayama and Hiroshima cut off for a fortnight; the count passes five hundred.

weather.line: The Camp Fire takes Paradise in six hours on a PG&E line. 85 dead; 18,804 buildings; the valley under smoke for a fortnight.
weather.unmade: The November wind does not come down the canyon. The line holds; Paradise sleeps.
weather.worse: The fire reaches Chico. The count passes two hundred; the utility files for bankruptcy that week.

weather.line: The Missouri at record height at 42 gauges after the March thaw. Offutt's runway under water; a million acres unplanted; the flooding runs to December.
weather.unmade: A slow thaw on the Missouri. The levees hold.
weather.worse: The Missouri and the Mississippi both. The Corn Belt unplanted to June; the levees gone from Omaha to St. Louis.

weather.line: The fire season opens in the drought and does not close. 24 million hectares; Sydney under smoke for weeks; 3,000 homes; 33 dead in the fires and 417 of the smoke; three billion animals.
weather.unmade: Rain on the eastern ranges in November. The fire season is ordinary.
weather.worse: The fires reach the Sydney suburbs and Canberra's edge. The count passes a hundred; the smoke over New Zealand.

weather.line: Salt up the Mekong further than in 2016. Five provinces in emergency; 33,000 hectares of rice lost; 70,000 households without fresh water.
weather.unmade: The upstream releases come early. The salt stops at the sea.
weather.worse: The salt reaches Can Tho itself. The winter rice gone across the delta; the orchards dead.

weather.line: The desert locust out of Arabia — Kenya's worst in seventy years, Ethiopia's and Somalia's in twenty-five. The Amhara teff gone; 2.25 million hectares by April; 20 million short of food.
weather.unmade: The Arabian breeding grounds dry out in 2019. The swarms never cross the Gulf of Aden.
weather.worse: Swarms across the whole Horn and into Pakistan. The FAO calls it a plague.

weather.line: The pneumonia out of Wuhan is declared a pandemic on 11 March. The borders close; the cities lock; 1.2 million dead in the United States, seven million on the world's confirmed count and eighteen million by the best estimate.
The Yangtze at flood from June. The Three Gorges reservoir at 167.85 metres, its highest; 63 million affected; 219 dead or missing; $32 billion.
weather.unmade: The plum rains end on time. The Three Gorges holds a normal summer.
weather.worse: The Three Gorges spilling at capacity for a month. Wuhan's river wall topped; the count passes a thousand.

weather.line: Verkhoyansk at 38 on 20 June — the hottest reading above the Arctic Circle. The Yakutian taiga burns through September; 14 million hectares; the permafrost gives.
weather.unmade: A cool June over the Lena. The fire season is short.
weather.worse: The taiga burns to the Laptev coast. Smoke over Alaska by August; the pipelines re-founded on melt.

weather.line: Arctic air to the Gulf. The Texas grid within minutes of collapse; 4.5 million dark; the refineries down; 246 dead on the state's count and perhaps 700.
weather.unmade: The cold front stalls in Oklahoma. Houston gets a frost.
weather.worse: The grid goes. Texas dark for a week; the count passes a thousand.

weather.line: No typhoon in 2020 and the worst drought in 56 years. Zengwen at eleven percent; Taichung's taps two days in seven; TSMC trucking water to the fabs.
weather.unmade: Winter rain over the island. The reservoirs hold; the fabs run.
weather.worse: The plum rains fail too. The fabs cut to half; the world's chip shortage deepens.

weather.line: The heat dome across the west — Lytton at 49.6 and then burned. Saskatoon at 40.5; grain elevators afire in Alberta; Manitoba declares an agricultural disaster on top of the drought.
weather.unmade: The ridge sits over the Pacific. A warm June on the Prairies.
weather.worse: The heat holds a fortnight. The wheat and canola gone across three provinces; the herds sold.

weather.line: 201.9 millimetres on Zhengzhou in an hour. Line 5 of the metro flooded with the passengers aboard; 398 dead, 139 of them at first concealed; $21 billion.
weather.unmade: The storm stalls over the mountains west of the city. Zhengzhou gets a wet evening.
weather.worse: The Yellow River dikes at Zhengzhou tested. The count is never agreed.

weather.line: The Ahr valley in flood on the night of 14 July. 196 dead in Germany, 39 in Belgium; €46 billion.
weather.unmade: The low drifts east into Poland. The Eifel gets rain.
weather.worse: The Ahr, the Erft and the Meuse together. The count passes five hundred.

weather.line: The fifth failed rains across the Horn — the driest in forty years. 9.5 million animals dead; 43,000 dead in Somalia in the year, half of them children under five.
weather.unmade: The Deyr rains come. The herds hold; the appeal is not made.
weather.worse: Famine declared across Somalia and the Ethiopian south. The count passes a hundred thousand.

weather.line: Lismore two metres above its record; Brisbane's suburbs under water again. 24 dead; A$9.6 billion.
weather.unmade: The east-coast low passes offshore. Rain on the northern rivers, and no more.
weather.worse: Lismore gone; Brisbane above the 2011 mark. The count passes a hundred.

weather.line: The monsoon over Sindh from June to October. A tenth of the country under water; 33 million affected; 1,739 dead; $40 billion.
weather.unmade: The monsoon over the Indus is heavy, and no more.
weather.worse: The Indus takes Sindh to the sea. The count passes five thousand.

weather.line: The driest year in five centuries, the Commission says. The Rhine at Emmerich below zero on the gauge; the Loire dry in July; the heat count 8,000 in Germany, 12,000 in France, 3,500 in Britain at 40.3.
weather.unmade: Rain on the plain in June. The Rhine runs; the harvest is ordinary.
weather.worse: The Rhine closed to barges through August. The count of the heat passes fifty thousand.

weather.line: The heat across Iberia and Italy from June. The Po dry; 30,000 hectares burned in Leiria; 11,000 dead in Spain, 18,000 in Italy.
weather.unmade: A hot Mediterranean summer, an ordinary one.
weather.worse: The heat runs to September. The Po dead to the sea; the count passes fifty thousand.

weather.line: Seventy days of heat over the Yangtze — Beibei at 45. The river at its lowest since 1961; Poyang a quarter its size; Sichuan's hydropower down and its factories with it.
weather.unmade: The Pacific high sits east. A hot summer on the Yangtze, and rain in July.
weather.worse: The heat runs into September. The Yangtze unnavigable; Sichuan dark; the count passes a hundred thousand.
